The construction is deterministic and never repeats an arc: four nodes at 1/1 pair up into two 2-cycles, drawn as bowed opposite arcs; 0/2, 1/1, 1/1, and 2/0 give two two-step paths from the source to the sink; and the five-node sequence uses one pair of opposite arcs." width="100%"} Node `i` gets exactly `in_degree_sequence[i]` incoming and `out_degree_sequence[i]` outgoing edges, with no self-loops and no repeated edges (a pair of nodes may still be joined once in each direction). The Kleitman-Wang algorithm, a directed Havel-Hakimi, repeatedly takes a node that still needs incoming edges, preferring the one with the most remaining out-degree, and gives it those edges from the nodes with the most remaining out-degree. It succeeds exactly when some simple directed graph has these degrees. If the two sequences differ in length, the shorter one is padded with zeros. There is no randomness: the same sequences always give the same graph. For a random graph with the same degrees, see `add_directed_configuration_model()`. The process follows NetworkX's `directed_havel_hakimi_graph()` and gives the same edges. In an undirected graph the same edges are added without their direction, so a pair joined both ways becomes two parallel edges and each node's degree is its in-degree plus its out-degree. The graph is appended without touching or connecting to existing nodes, and the whole construction is recorded as a single step. Directed Havel-Hakimi graphs are useful for: - checking that a pair of in- and out-degree sequences can be realized - a deterministic starting point for degree-preserving rewiring of directed graphs - directed test graphs with exactly prescribed degrees and no self-loops ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [in_degree_sequence]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [list[int]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : In-degree of each new node, as a list of non-negative integers. [out_degree_sequence]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [list[int]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Out-degree of each new node, as a list of non-negative integers. Must have the same sum as `in_degree_sequence=`. [type]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional value stored in the `type` attribute of every new node. If `None` (default), no `type` attribute is set. [label]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[True]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True` (default), each new node is labelled with its node ID as a string; a label that is already used raises `ValueError` before anything is added. If `False`, the nodes are left unlabelled. [rel]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional value stored in the `rel` attribute of every new edge. If `None` (default), no `rel` attribute is set. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Self for method chaining. The graph is modified in place. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If either sequence contains a negative entry, the two sums differ, or no simple directed graph has these degrees. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} A source, two relays, and a sink: ::: {#5da0ae85 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ec.Graph(directed=True).add_directed_havel_hakimi_graph( in_degree_sequence=[0, 1, 2, 3], out_degree_sequence=[3, 2, 1, 0], ) graph.get_edges_str_repr() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` ['1->2', '1->3', '1->4', '2->3', '2->4', '3->4'] ``` ::: ::: The sequences can't ask for a self-loop: a lone node can't point to itself. ::: {#2ffd7956 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} try: ec.Graph(directed=True).add_directed_havel_hakimi_graph([1], [1]) except ValueError as err: print(err) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` the in- and out-degree sequences are not digraphical: no simple directed graph has these degrees ``` ::: :::
